claims.behaviour: `AttributeCachingStrategy` has exactly four constants in this declaration order: `SHOULD`, `MAY`, `SHOULD_NOT`, `MUST_NOT` (ordinals 0 to 3).

`AttributeCachingStrategy.guessCachingStrategy(spec)` returns `MAY` when the spec's format id is the id of one of the standard formats of `ValueFormat` (html, text, number, boolean, duration, time, json, jsonArray, order, id, any), including a separately constructed `ValueFormat` that reuses such an id; for any other format id (e.g. `new ValueFormat<>("custom", String.class)`) it returns `SHOULD_NOT`. A null spec throws NullPointerException.
`AttributeContextDependency` has exactly six constants in this order: `USER`, `USER_LOCALE`, `USER_TIMEZONE`, `STRUCTURE`, `CURRENT_TIME`, `TRAIL`.

`AttributeContextDependency.guessContextDependencies(spec)` returns a set containing only `USER` when the spec's format equals `ValueFormat.HTML` (format equality is by format id, so a separately constructed format with id `html` also counts), and returns null for every other format (e.g. `ValueFormat.TEXT`, `ValueFormat.NUMBER`).

`AttributeContextDependency.union(set, additional...)` returns a new mutable set (adding to it works and does not affect the argument) containing every element of `set` plus every non-null element of the varargs. A null `set` is treated as empty, a null varargs array is ignored, null elements are skipped; `union(null)` with no extras returns an empty set, never null. The input set is not modified.

A minimal `AttributeLoader` implementation that only implements `getAttributeSpec()` reports: `getAttributeDependencies()` null; `getGlobalTrail()` null; `getContextDependencies()` equal to `AttributeContextDependency.guessContextDependencies(spec)` (a set with `USER` for an HTML spec, null otherwise); `getCachingStrategy()` equal to `AttributeCachingStrategy.guessCachingStrategy(spec)` (`MAY` for standard formats, `SHOULD_NOT` otherwise).

The default `AttributeLoaderContext.getDependencyValue(spec)` returns `getDependencyAttributeValue(spec).getValue()`: the plain value for a defined dependency value and null for an undefined or error value.

The default `AttributeLoaderContext.addTrail(ItemIdentity)` calls the abstract `addTrail(TrailItemSet)` exactly once with `TrailItemSet.of(item)`: a one-item set for a non-null item, and the empty set `TrailItemSet.None.NONE` for a null item.

`AttributeLoaders.issueLoader(spec)` returns a new item loader builder with the spec set, restricted to the single item type `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-issue` and with item class `com.atlassian.jira.issue.Issue`. A loader built from it with `valueFunction(...)` reports `isItemTypeSupported` true only for that exact type string, and resolves the item through `ItemAttributeContext.getItem(Issue.class)`; an item that does not resolve gets the undefined value without calling the function.

Building an `AttributeLoaders.issueLoader(spec)` builder after choosing an identity-based value function (`valueFunctionII` or `valueFunctionIIAV`) throws IllegalArgumentException from `build()`, because those forms do not accept the preset item class.

`AttributeLoaders` is a final subclass of `SharedAttributeLoaders` with a private constructor, so the inherited static factories (`itemLoader`, `derivedLoader`, `constantLoader`, `singleRowLoader`) are callable through it.
The default `ItemAttributeLoader.preload(itemIds, context)` does nothing (no exception, no interaction with the arguments).

`MultiRowAttributeLoader.getCachingStrategy()` defaults to `AttributeCachingStrategy.SHOULD` regardless of the spec's format; the aggregate, propagate and scanning loader interfaces inherit this default (e.g. an `AbstractPropagateLoader` subclass with an HTML or a custom-format spec reports `SHOULD`). Its context dependencies default stays the format-based guess.

`PropagateAttributeContext.Parent.isLoadingSuperRoot()` defaults to `getParent() == null`. `isLoadingRoots()` defaults to true only when `getParent()` is non-null and its `getRowId()` is -1; it is false for a null parent and for any other row id.
`PropagateAttributeLoader.isLoadingSuperRoot()` defaults to false; as a multi-row loader its default caching strategy is `SHOULD`, `preload` does nothing and `isWholeForestDependent()` is false.
`RowAttributeLoader.preload(rowIds, forest, context)` defaults to doing nothing and `isWholeForestDependent()` defaults to false.

`SharedAttributeLoaders.itemLoader(spec)` returns a new `ItemAttributeLoaderBuilder` with the spec set and no item type restriction or item class; a loader built from it with an identity-based value function reports `isItemTypeSupported` true for every type. Each call returns a distinct builder.

`SharedAttributeLoaders.derivedLoader(spec)` returns a `DerivedAttributeLoaderBuilder` with the spec set and no dependencies; `derivedLoader(spec, dep)` returns a `UniDerivedAttributeLoaderBuilder` with spec and dependency set (its built loader's dependencies are exactly `{dep}`); `derivedLoader(spec, x, y)` returns a `BiDerivedAttributeLoaderBuilder` with both dependencies set (built loader's dependencies `{x, y}`).

`SharedAttributeLoaders.constantLoader(spec, value)` returns a `DerivedAttributeLoaderBuilder` whose value function is already set: `build()` succeeds directly, and the loader's `loadValue(context)` returns the very same `AttributeValue` instance given (for any context, even null), with `getAttributeDependencies()` null. Further builder settings (dependencies, caching strategy) may still be added before `build()`.
`SharedAttributeLoaders.singleRowLoader(spec)` returns a new `SingleRowAttributeLoaderBuilder` with the spec set.

`TrailItemSet.of()` with no items, `of` of a collection that is empty or contains only nulls, and `of((Collection) null)` all return the shared constant `TrailItemSet.None.NONE` (same instance); `isEmpty()` is true for it. `of((ItemIdentity[]) null)` throws NullPointerException.

`TrailItemSet.of(x)` (or `of(x, x)`, duplicates collapse) returns a `TrailItemSet.OneItem` whose `getItem()` is `x`; `contains(x)` is true, `contains` of a different item (even of the same item type) is false, `contains(null)` is false; `isEmpty()` is false.

`TrailItemSet.of` with 2 to 50 distinct non-null items returns a `TrailItemSet.SpecificItems` holding exactly those items (nulls dropped): `getItems()` equals that set and is unmodifiable (adding throws UnsupportedOperationException); `contains` is true exactly for those items and false for other items and for null.

When `TrailItemSet.of` receives more than 50 distinct items (default item limit), the result is reduced to the items' item types: a `TrailItemSet.OneType` if all have the same type, a `TrailItemSet.SpecificTypes` for 2 to 10 types, and `TrailItemSet.AllItems.ALL_ITEMS` for more than 10 types. The reduced set then reports `contains` true for any item of a covered type, including items never added.

Defect kept from the original: when `TrailItemSet.of` gets input whose only distinct non-null item is `x` but the first element is null (e.g. `of(null, x)` or `of(Arrays.asList(null, x))`), it returns a `TrailItemSet.OneItem` built from the first element, so `getItem()` returns null and `contains(x)` is false (as the original does).

`TrailItemSet.ofTypes(types)`: null input, an empty collection or only nulls give `TrailItemSet.None.NONE`; null elements are ignored and duplicates collapse; one distinct type gives a `TrailItemSet.OneType` with that `getItemType()`; 2 to 10 types give a `TrailItemSet.SpecificTypes` whose `getTypes()` is exactly those types (unmodifiable); 11 or more types give `TrailItemSet.AllItems.ALL_ITEMS`.

The item limit (default 50) and type limit (default 10) used by `TrailItemSet` factories, `expand` and `union` are read once, when the class is initialised, through `DarkFeatures.getInteger` with keys `structure.trail.itemLimit` and `structure.trail.typeLimit` (an application property if set, otherwise a JVM system property of that name, otherwise the default).

`TrailItemSet.containsAny(collection)` returns false for a null or empty collection and otherwise true iff `contains` is true for at least one element (null elements simply do not match, except for the all-items set, which contains null too).
`TrailItemSet.isEmpty()` is true only for the empty form (`TrailItemSet.None`); one-item, item-set, type-level and all-items sets all report false.

`TrailItemSet.equals` compares form and content regardless of how the set was built: `of(x)` equals `TrailItemSet.None.NONE.expand(x)`; `of(x, y)` equals `of(y, x)` and `of(x).expand(y)`; `ofTypes(["a"])` equals `ofTypes(["a", null])`; `NONE` equals a separately constructed `new TrailItemSet.None()` and `ALL_ITEMS` equals `new TrailItemSet.AllItems()`. An item-level set never equals a type-level set (even with the same type), a one-item set never equals a two-item set, and no trail set equals null or a non-trail object.
`TrailItemSet.hashCode()` is equal for equal sets, is never 0, and is stable across calls (computed once and cached).

`TrailItemSet.toString()` gives `{}` for the empty set and `{ALL}` for the all-items set; for other forms it prints the type list and item list (each comma-joined, in hash order) inside braces with a comma always placed between the two lists even when one is empty, e.g. a one-type set of `t` prints `{t,}` and a one-item set prints `{,` + the item's `toString()` + `}` (as the original does).

`TrailItemSet` instances are never changed by `expand` or `union`: the receiver and the argument keep their content (`contains`, `equals`) after these calls; any widening is returned as a new or different set.

`TrailItemSet.None.NONE`: `contains` is false for every argument including null; `expand(null)` returns `NONE` itself and `expand(x)` returns a one-item set of `x`; `union(null)` returns `NONE`, `union(s)` returns `s` itself (same instance); `accept(visitor)` calls `visitor.visitNone()` only.

`TrailItemSet.AllItems.ALL_ITEMS`: `contains` is true for any argument including null; `expand(anything)` and `union(anything, including null)` return `ALL_ITEMS` itself; `accept(visitor)` calls `visitor.visitAll()` only.

`TrailItemSet.OneItem.expand(i)` returns the same instance for null or for its own item, and otherwise a `TrailItemSet.SpecificItems` holding both items. `accept(visitor)` calls `visitor.visit(OneItem)` with this set.

`TrailItemSet.OneItem.union(other)` returns this set for null; otherwise it is `other.expand(heldItem)`: with `NONE` it returns a set equal to this one, with `ALL_ITEMS` it returns `ALL_ITEMS`, with a type-level set covering the item's type it returns that type-level set itself, with a type-level set not covering it a type-level set with the item's type added, and with an item-level set the combined items.

`TrailItemSet.SpecificItems.expand(i)` returns the same instance when `i` is null or already held; otherwise a set with `i` added: still a `TrailItemSet.SpecificItems` while the total stays at or below 50 items, and reduced to type level (one type, several types, or all items past 10 types) once it would exceed 50.

`TrailItemSet.SpecificItems.union(other)`: null or the `NONE` constant returns this set; the `ALL_ITEMS` constant returns `ALL_ITEMS`; a type-level argument returns a type-level set covering the argument's types plus the item types of this set's items; an item-level argument returns `TrailItemSet.of` of the combined items (exact up to 50, reduced to types beyond).

Defect kept from the original: `TrailItemSet.SpecificItems.union` recognises the empty and all-items sets only by identity with `NONE` / `ALL_ITEMS`; passing a separately constructed `new TrailItemSet.None()` or `new TrailItemSet.AllItems()` throws NullPointerException (as the original does).

`TrailItemSet.OneType`: `contains(i)` is true iff `i` is non-null and its item type equals the covered type; `expand(i)` returns the same instance for null or an item of the covered type, otherwise a `TrailItemSet.SpecificTypes` of both types; `accept(visitor)` calls `visitor.visit(OneType)`.

`TrailItemSet.OneType.union(other)`: null or `NONE` returns this set; an item-level argument (one item or several) gives a type-level set covering this type plus the items' types (for a single item of the covered type the very same set is returned; for several items all of the covered type an equal set); `ALL_ITEMS` gives `ALL_ITEMS`; another `OneType` of the same type returns this set, of a different type a two-type set; a `SpecificTypes` argument gives the union of types (all items past 10 types).

`TrailItemSet.SpecificTypes`: `contains(i)` is true iff `i` is non-null and its item type is one of `getTypes()`; `expand(i)` returns the same instance for null or an item of a covered type, otherwise a set with that type added (`ALL_ITEMS` once more than 10 types); `union` follows the same rules as for `OneType` (item-level arguments widened to their types, `NONE`/null give this set, `ALL_ITEMS` gives `ALL_ITEMS`, a `OneType` already covered gives this set); `accept(visitor)` calls `visitor.visit(SpecificTypes)`.

`TrailItemSet.Collector.collect(set)` returns a collector filled from the set: for `NONE` `getItems()` and `getTypes()` are null and `isAll()` false; for item-level sets `getItems()` holds the items and `getTypes()` is null; for type-level sets `getTypes()` holds the types and `getItems()` is null; for `ALL_ITEMS` `isAll()` is true and both getters return null. A null argument throws NullPointerException.

Two `TrailItemSet.Collector`s are equal (with equal hash codes) iff their item sets, type sets and all-items flag are equal; `toString()` of a collector is the same text as `toString()` of the trail set it was collected from (`{ALL}` when the all flag is set).

Calling `visitItem`, `visitType` or `visitAll` directly on a collector adds the item to its item set, the type to its type set, or sets `isAll()`; when the collector had no set of that kind (e.g. `visitType` on a collector from an item-level set), an AssertionError is thrown if assertions are enabled, otherwise the set is created and the value recorded.

`TrailItemSet.ReadVisitor` defaults: `visitNone()` does nothing; `visit(OneItem)` calls `visitItem` once with the item; `visit(SpecificItems)` calls `visitItem` once per held item; `visit(OneType)` calls `visitType` once with the type; `visit(SpecificTypes)` calls `visitType` once per type. Only `visitItem`, `visitType` and `visitAll` must be implemented.

`TrailItemSet.accept(visitor)` calls exactly one `TrailItemSet.Visitor` method, once: `visitNone` for the empty set, `visit(OneItem)`, `visit(SpecificItems)`, `visit(OneType)`, `visit(SpecificTypes)` with the set itself, or `visitAll` for the all-items set.
Constructing any `AbstractAttributeLoader` subclass with a null spec throws IllegalArgumentException with message `null spec`.

`AbstractAttributeLoader.getAttributeSpec()` returns the exact spec instance passed to the constructor (and is final); the other `AttributeLoader` defaults are unchanged (dependencies null, global trail null, context dependencies and caching strategy guessed from the spec's format).
`AbstractAttributeLoader.toString()` returns the runtime class's fully qualified name (`getClass().getName()`) followed by `(`, the spec's `toString()`, and `)`.

`AbstractAggregateLoader.firstChildError(list)` returns the first element (same instance) whose `isError()` is true, skipping null elements; it returns null when no element is an error (including for an empty list and for lists of defined or plain undefined values). A null list throws NullPointerException.
An `AbstractAggregateLoader` subclass is an `AggregateAttributeLoader`: a null spec throws IllegalArgumentException, and its default caching strategy is `SHOULD`.

An `AbstractDerivedAttributeLoader` subclass is a `DerivedAttributeLoader` holding the given spec; a null spec throws IllegalArgumentException (`null spec`). Caching strategy and context dependencies are the format-based defaults.
An `AbstractItemAttributeLoader` subclass is an `ItemAttributeLoader` holding the given spec; a null spec throws IllegalArgumentException (`null spec`); `preload` does nothing by default.

An `AbstractPropagateLoader` subclass is a `PropagateAttributeLoader` holding the given spec; a null spec throws IllegalArgumentException (`null spec`); defaults: caching strategy `SHOULD`, `isLoadingSuperRoot()` false, `isWholeForestDependent()` false.

An `AbstractSingleRowAttributeLoader` subclass is a `SingleRowAttributeLoader` holding the given spec; a null spec throws IllegalArgumentException (`null spec`); caching strategy is the format-based default (not `SHOULD`).

`AbstractNaiveDistinctAggregateLoader.loadValue(children, ctx)` collects into one map the item-to-value maps carried as loader data (`getLoaderData(Map.class)`) by every defined child value; undefined and error children, and defined children without such data, contribute nothing (child errors are not propagated). When two children carry the same item, the later child's entry wins.

`AbstractNaiveDistinctAggregateLoader.loadValue` adds the current row's item (`ctx.getRow().getItemId()`) with the value of `getRowValue(ctx)` only if that item is not already in the merged map and the value is non-null; if the item is already present `getRowValue` is not called at all, so an item occurring several times in the subtree is counted once.

`AbstractNaiveDistinctAggregateLoader.loadValue` returns a defined value equal to `combine(values of the merged map, ctx)` that carries the merged map as loader data; that map is unmodifiable. Example: children carrying {A:1,B:2} and {B:2,C:3} on a row of item D with own value 4 and a summing `combine` give 10 with data {A:1,B:2,C:3,D:4}. If `combine` returns null, an AssertionError is thrown when assertions are enabled, otherwise the result is an undefined value carrying the map.
A null element in the children list passed to `AbstractNaiveDistinctAggregateLoader.loadValue` causes a NullPointerException.

`AbstractScanningLoader` reads spec parameters at construction: `baseLevel` (integer, absent means 0, negative clamped to 0) is returned by `getBaseLevel()`; `levels` (list of 1-based level numbers) is converted to 0-based depths, sorted ascending, de-duplicated, and depths below the base level removed, and returned by `getLevelsSorted()` (null when the parameter is absent). Example: `levels` [3,1,1] with no base level gives [0,2]; `levels` [1,2,3] with `baseLevel` 2 gives [2].

`AbstractScanningLoader.isAboveBaseLevel(ctx)` is true iff the base level is above 0 and `ctx.getDepth()` is less than it; `isLevelSkipped(ctx)` is true iff a `levels` parameter was given and `ctx.getDepth()` is not one of the converted depths; `isRowSkipped` returns false by default.
`AbstractScanningLoader.loadValue` returns the plain undefined value (no loader data) for a row above the base level, without calling `loadValueForPassingRow`.

For a row skipped by level or by `isRowSkipped`, `AbstractScanningLoader.loadValue` returns `carryPrecedingValueForSkippedRow(preceding)`: if the preceding value is defined, an undefined value whose loader data is the preceding plain value; otherwise the preceding value object itself (an error stays an error, a carried undefined stays carried). `loadValueForPassingRow` is not called.

For a contributing row, `AbstractScanningLoader.loadValue` calls `loadValueForPassingRow(running, ctx)` where `running` is the preceding value's plain value if defined, otherwise the value it carries as loader data (null when none). If the new value equals `running` and the preceding value is defined, the preceding value object itself is returned; otherwise `AttributeValue.ofNullable(newValue)` (undefined for null).

An error preceding value carries no running value: for the next contributing row `AbstractScanningLoader` passes null as the running value to `loadValueForPassingRow`, so the running total restarts rather than propagating the error.
`AbstractScanningLoader` subclasses are scanning loaders with default caching strategy `SHOULD`; a null spec throws IllegalArgumentException.
`InheritedValueLoader.getAttributeDependencies()` returns a singleton set holding the value spec (constructor argument 2); `getAttributeSpec()` is argument 1; caching strategy defaults to `SHOULD`.

With `forceParentValue` false, the function returned by `InheritedValueLoader.loadChildren(parentValue, parent)` (never null) returns, for each child, the child's own value of the dependency (`ctx.getDependencyAttributeValue(valueSpec)`, same instance) when it is defined, and otherwise the parent value instance passed to `loadChildren` (which may itself be undefined or an error).

With `forceParentValue` true, the function returned by `InheritedValueLoader.loadChildren` returns the parent value for every child whenever the parent value is defined; only when the parent value is not defined does a child's own defined dependency value win (else the parent value is returned).

`ItemTypeAttributeLoader(spec, types...)` throws IllegalArgumentException `empty or null item types` for a null or empty varargs (a null spec is rejected first with `null spec`). `isItemTypeSupported(t)` (final) is true exactly for the given type strings (duplicates collapse); the protected `myItemTypes` is an unmodifiable set of them.

`ItemClassAttributeLoader(spec, itemClass, types...)` checks the spec (`null spec`), then the item types (`empty or null item types`), then the class: a null class throws IllegalArgumentException `item class is not defined`.

`ItemClassAttributeLoader.loadValue(itemId, ctx)` calls `ctx.getItem(itemClass)`; if that returns null it returns the plain undefined value without calling `getValue`; otherwise it returns `getValue(item, ctx)` unchanged (a null result is returned as null).

An `IssueAttributeLoader` subclass supports exactly the item type `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-issue` (`isItemTypeSupported` false for any other string) and resolves items with `ctx.getItem(com.atlassian.jira.issue.Issue.class)`, returning the undefined value when it is null and otherwise `getValue(issue, ctx)`. A null spec throws IllegalArgumentException.

`LongSumLoader.reduce(list)` returns the sum of the non-null elements as a `Long`, or null when the list is empty or holds only nulls (e.g. [1, null, 2] gives 3; [null] gives null). Overflow wraps silently (`Long.MAX_VALUE` + 1 gives `Long.MIN_VALUE`).

`LongSumLoader(spec, dependency)`: `getAttributeDependencies()` is a singleton of the dependency; the row's own value is the dependency's value from the context; the reduction strategy comes from the spec's `type` parameter (default `subtree`: row's own value plus the totals of its children, e.g. own 5 with children totals 3 and null gives 8). Its merge operations use the inherited `ValueReducer` defaults.

A new `NumberAccumulator` (and one that only received null via `add`, `remove`, `addMultiply` or `removeMultiply`) has `toNumber()` null, `toValue()` equal to the plain undefined value, and `toString()` exactly `NumberAccumulator[]`.

While every added number is integral, `NumberAccumulator.toNumber()` returns a `Long` with exact long arithmetic, whatever the input types (`Integer`, `Short`, `Long`, or a `Double`/`Float` whose value is a whole number such as 2.0): e.g. add(1), add(2) gives `Long` 3 and `toString()` `NumberAccumulator[3L]`; add(Double 2.0) gives `Long` 2. Long overflow wraps.

Once a non-integral `Number` (other than `BigDecimal`/`BigInteger`) is added, `NumberAccumulator.toNumber()` returns a `Double` holding the sum of everything added so far, including earlier integral values (add(1), add(0.5) gives 1.5; `toString()` `NumberAccumulator[1.5D]`). The double sum uses compensated summation, so adding 0.1 ten times gives exactly 1.0.

Once a `BigDecimal` or `BigInteger` is added, `NumberAccumulator` switches permanently to `BigDecimal` arithmetic with `MathContext.DECIMAL64` (16 significant digits): the previous total is converted (a fractional double via `new BigDecimal(double, DECIMAL64)`), later primitives are converted the same way, and `toNumber()` returns a `BigDecimal` with trailing zeros stripped (add(new BigDecimal("1.50")), add(1) gives 2.5; add(0.5), add(BigInteger.ONE) gives 1.5; add(0.1) after a big value contributes exactly 0.1). `toString()` shows the plain decimal, e.g. `NumberAccumulator[100]` for a total of 100 whose `toNumber()` is `1E+2`.

In `BigDecimal` mode each `NumberAccumulator` addition is rounded to 16 significant digits (e.g. adding `new BigDecimal("12345678901234567")` to an empty accumulator gives a total numerically equal to 12345678901234570).

`NumberAccumulator.remove(n)` subtracts n, `addMultiply(n, k)` adds n times k (k may be negative or 0), `removeMultiply(n, k)` subtracts n times k. Any non-null number marks the accumulator defined even if the total is zero: add(5), remove(5) gives `Long` 0; addMultiply(7, 0) gives `Long` 0; addMultiply(2.5, 3) gives `Double` 7.5; removeMultiply(2, 3) gives `Long` -6. Null numbers are ignored.
`NumberAccumulator.toValue()` returns `AttributeValue.ofNullable(toNumber())`: a defined value with the current total once anything non-null was added.

`NumberSumLoader.reduce(list)` sums the non-null numbers with `NumberAccumulator` semantics and returns null when there are none: [1, 2] of `Integer` gives `Long` 3; [1, 0.5] gives `Double` 1.5; [1, `BigDecimal` 2.50] gives `BigDecimal` 3.5; [] and [null] give null.

`NumberSumLoader.merge(selfSupplier, reducedSupplier)` returns the accumulated sum of the two supplied numbers, ignoring nulls (null when both are null); `merge(selfSupplier, list)` returns the sum of the supplied self number and all non-null list elements (null when all are null). Each supplier is called exactly once.

`NumberSumLoader(spec, dependency)` declares exactly `{dependency}` as attribute dependencies, uses the dependency's value as the row's own value and the spec's `type` parameter for the reduction strategy; an unknown `type` makes the constructor throw IllegalArgumentException.

`ScanningLongSumLoader` produces a running total of its `Long` dependency in scanning order: each contributing row's value is the running value plus the row's dependency value, nulls ignored, null (undefined) when both are null. With dependency values 1, 2, null, 4 on consecutive contributing rows (first preceding value undefined) the results are 1, 3, 3 (the preceding value object itself), 7. `getAttributeDependencies()` is a singleton of the dependency.

`ScanningNumberSumLoader` produces a running total of its `Number` dependency with `NumberAccumulator` semantics: `Integer` 1 then 2 give `Long` 1 then `Long` 3; adding 0.5 next gives `Double` 3.5; nulls are ignored and the result is undefined while nothing was accumulated. `getAttributeDependencies()` is a singleton of the dependency.

`SimpleAttributeProvider.create(loaders...)` returns a provider whose `createAttributeLoader(spec, ctx)` returns null when no loader was registered with the requested spec's id; otherwise it considers only registered loaders whose spec parameters are all present with equal values in the requested spec's parameters, and returns null if none qualifies. The context argument is not used.

Among qualifying loaders, `SimpleAttributeProvider.createAttributeLoader` returns the one whose spec has the most parameters; ties are broken in favour of a loader whose spec format equals the requested format, and remaining ties by registration order (first registered wins). Example: loaders for id `x` with params {} and {a:1}; a request for `x` with {a:1, b:2} gets the {a:1} loader, a request with {a:2} gets the {} loader.

`SimpleAttributeProvider.registerLoader` files a loader under its spec's id (several per id allowed); `create` with a null loader element throws NullPointerException. `registerCompositeLoader(spec, loaders...)` registers one composite loader built by `CompositeAttributeLoader.create` for the given spec (served for that spec's id); with no loaders it throws IllegalArgumentException `empty or null loaders`.

`SimpleDerivedAttributeLoader.getAttributeDependencies()` (final) returns a singleton set holding the dependency spec; the protected `myDependency` field holds it. The two-argument constructor turns yield on.

With yield on, `SimpleDerivedAttributeLoader.loadValue(ctx)` returns null when the dependency value has no plain value (undefined or error), without calling `getValue`; when `getValue` returns null it also returns null; otherwise it returns a new defined value holding `getValue`'s result.

With yield off, when the dependency value has no plain value, `SimpleDerivedAttributeLoader.loadValue` returns the dependency's `AttributeValue` object itself (an error stays an error, loader data is kept); when `getValue` returns null it returns the plain undefined value.

`SimpleDerivedAttributeLoader.idLoader(spec, dependency)` returns null unless both specs hold the very same `ValueFormat` instance (an equal but separately constructed format also gives null); otherwise it returns a derived loader with yield on whose value is a new defined value equal to the dependency's plain value (null result, i.e. yielding, when the dependency has no value).

Every setter of the loader builders (`spec`, `contextDependency`, `contextDependencies`, `noContextDependencies`, `cachingStrategy`, `globalTrail`, and the kind-specific setters) returns the same builder instance it was called on; `spec` replaces an earlier spec.

Builder context dependencies: when none were set the built loader's `getContextDependencies()` is the format-based default (a set with `USER` for an HTML spec, null otherwise). `contextDependency(d)` / `contextDependencies(d...)` add to the declared set (null array and null elements ignored); the built loader then returns exactly the added set, as an unmodifiable copy (later builder changes do not affect it).

`noContextDependencies()` makes the built loader report an empty context dependency set (overriding e.g. the `USER` default of an HTML spec) and discards dependencies added before. Defect kept from the original: calling `contextDependency` with a non-null value afterwards (or a trail setter that adds `TRAIL`) throws UnsupportedOperationException (as the original does).

`cachingStrategy(s)` makes the built loader return `s` from `getCachingStrategy()`; when never set or set to null the loader returns the format-based guess (`MAY` for standard formats, `SHOULD_NOT` otherwise).

Builder `globalTrail(TrailItemSet)` accumulates: the first call stores the given set (same instance), later calls store the union with the previous trail; null is ignored. `globalTrail(ItemIdentity)` adds `TrailItemSet.of(item)`, so a null item still sets the empty set `NONE` when nothing was set before. Without any call the built loader's `getGlobalTrail()` is null.

The protected static helpers of `AttributeLoaderBuilder`: `notNull(v, name)` returns `v` or throws IllegalArgumentException with message `null ` + name (e.g. `null attributeSpec`); `nullableCollectionOfNonNulls(coll, name)` returns the same collection (null allowed) or throws IllegalArgumentException `null ` + name + `[` + index + `]` for the first null element (e.g. `null dependencies[1]`).

`dependency(spec)` / `dependencies(specs...)` add attribute dependencies in first-added order with duplicates collapsed; null arrays and null elements are ignored. The built loader's `getAttributeDependencies()` is an unmodifiable copy in that order, or null when nothing was ever added (not an empty set).

`BaseAttributeLoader` returns the spec, dependency set, context dependency set, caching strategy and global trail given to its constructor (same instances); each one given as null falls back to the `AttributeLoader` default (dependencies null, context dependencies and caching strategy guessed from the spec's format, global trail null). A null spec is not rejected at construction.
`BaseDerivedAttributeLoader.loadValue(ctx)` returns exactly what the loading function returns for that context (including null); the other getters behave as in `BaseAttributeLoader`.

`BaseItemAttributeLoader.isItemTypeSupported(t)` is true for every type when the predicate is null, otherwise the predicate's answer; `loadValue(item, ctx)` returns the value function's result unchanged (including null).
`BaseItemAttributeLoader.preload(ids, ctx)` passes the same collection and context to the preload callback when one was given, and does nothing when it is null.

`BaseSingleRowAttributeLoader.loadValue(row, ctx)` returns the loading function's result unchanged (including null); `preload(rowIds, forest, ctx)` forwards the same arguments to the `RowPreloadFunction` if one was given, else does nothing; `isWholeForestDependent()` returns the constructor flag.

`DerivedAttributeLoaderBuilder` value function forms (the last call wins): `valueFunctionAV(Function<ctx, AttributeValue>)` result returned as is (null stays null); `valueFunctionAV(Supplier)` likewise, ignoring the context; `valueFunction(Function<ctx, T>)` and `valueFunction(Supplier<T>)` wrap the plain result with `AttributeValue.ofNullable` (null becomes the undefined value, never null).

`DerivedAttributeLoaderBuilder.build()` returns a `BaseDerivedAttributeLoader` carrying the builder's spec, dependencies, context dependencies, caching strategy and global trail. Without a spec it throws IllegalArgumentException `null attributeSpec`; without a value function, `null valueFunction` (spec is checked first).

`UniDerivedAttributeLoaderBuilder.build()` returns a `UniDerivedAttributeLoaderBuilder.BuiltDerivedLoader` (a `SimpleDerivedAttributeLoader`) whose dependencies are exactly `{dependency}`. It throws IllegalArgumentException, checked in this order, `null attributeSpec`, `null dependencySpec`, `null derivationFunction` when the spec, dependency or value function is missing.

A loader from `UniDerivedAttributeLoaderBuilder` yields by default: it returns null when the dependency has no plain value (the value function is not called) or when the function returns null. After `yieldOnNull(false)` it returns the dependency's own `AttributeValue` object when that has no plain value (an error stays an error) and the undefined value when the function returns null. A non-null result is returned as a defined value.
`UniDerivedAttributeLoaderBuilder.valueFunction(BiFunction)` receives the dependency's non-null plain value and the derived context; the `Function` form receives only the value. The last call wins.

`UniDerivedAttributeLoaderBuilder.trail(f)` with non-null `f` adds `TRAIL` to the builder's context dependencies (so for an HTML spec the built loader declares only `{TRAIL}`, not `USER`); the built loader calls `f` with the dependency's non-null value before the value function and, if `f` returns a non-null item, reports it through `ctx.addTrail(item)`. `trail(null)` clears the function without removing `TRAIL`.

`UniDerivedAttributeLoaderBuilder.BuiltDerivedLoader` returns the context dependencies, caching strategy and global trail given to it, each falling back to the format-based default (or null global trail) when null was given.

`BiDerivedAttributeLoaderBuilder.build()` returns a `BiDerivedAttributeLoaderBuilder.BuiltBiDerivedLoader` whose `getAttributeDependencies()` is an immutable set of the x and y specs (a single element when they are equal). Missing settings throw IllegalArgumentException, checked in order: `null attributeSpec`, `null xDependency`, `null yDependency`, `null derivationFunction`. `dependencies(x, y)` sets both, `xDependency`/`yDependency` set one each.

A loader from `BiDerivedAttributeLoaderBuilder` reads both dependency values; if both plain values are non-null it applies the value function: a non-null result becomes a defined value, a null result gives null (yield, the default) or the undefined value after `yieldOnNull(false)`. If either plain value is null (undefined or error), the function is not called and the result is null (yield) or the plain undefined value (no yield); input errors are not propagated.

`xTrail(f)` / `yTrail(g)` with non-null functions add `TRAIL` to the builder's context dependencies; when both inputs are non-null the built loader calls `f(x)` then `g(y)` before the value function and reports each non-null returned item via `ctx.addTrail(item)`.

`BiDerivedAttributeLoaderBuilder.BuiltBiDerivedLoader` returns the given context dependencies and caching strategy, each falling back to the format-based default when null, and the given global trail or null.

`ItemAttributeLoaderBuilder.itemType(types...)` restricts the built loader's `isItemTypeSupported` to exactly the given strings (replacing an earlier restriction); no arguments throw IllegalArgumentException `need at least one item type`, a null element throws IllegalArgumentException `itemType cannot be null`, a null array throws NullPointerException. `anyItemType()` removes the restriction (every type supported, also the default).

`ItemAttributeLoaderBuilder.itemClass(c)` returns the same builder instance (retyped) and sets the class items are resolved to; `itemClass(null)` throws IllegalArgumentException `null itemClass` immediately.

With `valueFunctionIIAV(f)` the built loader returns `f(itemId, ctx)` unchanged (including null). `valueFunctionIIAV((BiFunction) null)` throws IllegalArgumentException `null loadingFunction` immediately; the one-argument `Function` form wraps the function, so a null there only fails with NullPointerException when a value is loaded.

With `valueFunctionII(f)` the built loader returns `AttributeValue.ofNullable(f(itemId, ctx))`; with `yieldOnNull()` a null result returns null instead of the undefined value; with `valueTrail(g)`, for a non-null value `g(value)` is called and a non-null item reported via `ctx.addTrail`. A null function passed to the `BiFunction` form makes `build()` throw IllegalArgumentException `null valueFunction`.

With `valueFunctionAV(f)` and an item class, the built loader resolves `ctx.getItem(itemClass)`; if null it returns the plain undefined value without calling `f`; otherwise it reports the `itemTrail` item (if set and non-null) via `ctx.addTrail` and returns `f(item, ctx)` unchanged (including null). `valueFunctionAV((BiFunction) null)` throws IllegalArgumentException `null itemLoadingFunction` immediately.

With `valueFunction(f)` and an item class, the built loader resolves `ctx.getItem(itemClass)`; if null it returns the plain undefined value without calling anything else; otherwise, in this order, it reports the `itemTrail` item (if non-null), reports the `trailItemSet` set (if non-null) via `ctx.addTrail(TrailItemSet)`, computes `f(item, ctx)`, and returns null for a null result with `yieldOnNull()`, else reports the `valueTrail` item for a non-null value and returns `AttributeValue.ofNullable(result)`. A null `BiFunction` makes `build()` throw IllegalArgumentException `null itemFunction`.

`ItemAttributeLoaderBuilder.build()` throws IllegalArgumentException for setting combinations the chosen value function form does not accept: `valueFunctionIIAV` accepts none of `itemClass`, `yieldOnNull`, `valueTrail`, `itemTrail`, `trailItemSet`; `valueFunctionAV` accepts `itemClass` and `itemTrail` only; `valueFunctionII` accepts `yieldOnNull` and `valueTrail` only; `valueFunction` accepts all. The item-resolving forms (`valueFunctionAV`, `valueFunction`) without an item class throw IllegalArgumentException `null itemClass`.

`ItemAttributeLoaderBuilder.build()` with no value function throws IllegalArgumentException `null loading function` (checked before the spec); with a value function but no spec it throws `null attributeSpec`. The last value function call wins.

`ItemAttributeLoaderBuilder.build()` returns a `BaseItemAttributeLoader` with the builder's dependencies, context dependencies, caching strategy, global trail, item type restriction and preload callback (`preload(cb)` forwards the item ids and context to `cb`; null means no-op).
`itemTrail`, `trailItemSet` and `valueTrail` with a non-null function each add `TRAIL` to the builder's context dependencies; with null they clear the function but leave any `TRAIL` already added.

`SingleRowAttributeLoaderBuilder` value function forms (last call wins): `valueFunctionAV(BiFunction<row, ctx, AttributeValue>)` and `valueFunctionAV(Function<row, AttributeValue>)` return the result as is (null stays null); `valueFunction(BiFunction<row, ctx, T>)` and `valueFunction(Function<row, T>)` wrap with `AttributeValue.ofNullable` (null becomes the undefined value).

`SingleRowAttributeLoaderBuilder.build()` returns a `BaseSingleRowAttributeLoader` with the builder's dependencies, context dependencies, caching strategy, global trail and preload callback; `isWholeForestDependent()` is true only after `dependsOnWholeForest()`. It throws IllegalArgumentException `null attributeSpec` without a spec and `null valueFunction` without a value function.

`LoaderType` constants in order with their kind interface and weight: `PROPAGATE` (`PropagateAttributeLoader`, 4), `AGGREGATE` (`AggregateAttributeLoader`, 4), `SCANNING` (`ScanningAttributeLoader`, 4), `SINGLE_ROW` (`SingleRowAttributeLoader`, 3), `ITEM` (`ItemAttributeLoader`, 2), `DERIVED` (`DerivedAttributeLoader`, 1), returned by `getLoaderClass()` and `getLoaderWeight()`.
`LoaderType.is(loader)` is true iff the loader is an instance of that constant's kind interface (e.g. `ITEM.is` of a built item loader is true, `DERIVED.is` of it false).

`LoaderType.getType(loader)` / `getType(Class)` return the first constant, in declaration order, whose kind interface is assignable from the class (`getType(SingleRowAttributeLoader.class)` is `SINGLE_ROW`, a built derived loader gives `DERIVED`). A class implementing none (e.g. `AttributeLoader.class`, `RowAttributeLoader.class`, `MultiRowAttributeLoader.class`, or a bare `AttributeLoader` lambda) throws IllegalArgumentException with message `Unsupported AttributeLoader type: ` followed by the class's `toString()`; a null loader throws NullPointerException. A class implementing two kinds fails with AssertionError when assertions are enabled, otherwise the first in declaration order wins.

`AttributeLoaderAdapter.adapt(loader, cls)` returns the loader itself (same instance) when the loader's kind equals the kind of `cls`; when `cls` is not a kind interface (e.g. `AttributeLoader.class`) or the loader has no kind, it throws IllegalArgumentException.

`AttributeLoaderAdapter.adapt` wraps the loader for these conversions only: derived to item, single-row, aggregate, propagate or scanning; item to single-row, aggregate, propagate or scanning; single-row to aggregate, propagate or scanning. Every other differing pair (anything to derived, a multi-row kind to anything else, item or single-row to item) throws IllegalArgumentException `unadaptable loaders`. The result is an instance of `cls`.

A loader returned wrapped by `AttributeLoaderAdapter.adapt` reports the wrapped loader's spec, attribute dependencies, context dependencies, caching strategy and global trail (so e.g. a derived loader adapted to `AggregateAttributeLoader` keeps the derived loader's caching strategy rather than `SHOULD`); its `toString()` is the adapter's class name, `:`, and the wrapped loader's text.

A derived loader adapted by `AttributeLoaderAdapter.adapt` ignores row, item, children and preceding values and returns `loadValue(ctx)` of the derived loader, using the given context as a `DerivedAttributeContext` (a context that is not one causes an AssertionError when assertions are enabled, otherwise ClassCastException). Adapted to item it supports every item type; adapted to propagate its `loadChildren` returns a non-null function and ignores the parent value.

An item loader adapted to a row kind by `AttributeLoaderAdapter.adapt` computes a row's value by treating the row context as an `ItemAttributeContext`: for the context's item id of a supported type it returns the item loader's `loadValue(itemId, ctx)`, for an unsupported type null. Its `preload(rowIds, forest, ctx)` scans the forest's existing rows among `rowIds` and calls the item loader's `preload` once with the set of their item ids whose type is supported. Its `isWholeForestDependent()` is false; adapted to propagate, `loadChildren` always returns a function.

A single-row loader adapted to aggregate or scanning by `AttributeLoaderAdapter.adapt` returns `loadValue(ctx.getRow(), ctx)` of the single-row loader (context used as a `SingleRowAttributeContext`) and forwards `preload` and `isWholeForestDependent`; adapted to propagate, `loadChildren` returns a function calling `loadValue(row, ctx)` for each child, but `preload` is a no-op and `isWholeForestDependent()` is false even when the wrapped loader says true (as the original does).

`CompositeAttributeLoader.create(spec, loaders)` throws IllegalArgumentException `empty or null loaders` for a null or empty list, and IllegalArgumentException (`Unsupported AttributeLoader type: ...`) if a loader is of no recognised kind.

`CompositeAttributeLoader.create` returns a new composite (never one of the given loaders, even for a single loader) whose kind is the kind of the highest-weight loader (the first one among equal weights) and whose `getAttributeSpec()` is the given spec. Lower-weight loaders are adapted to that kind; loaders that cannot be (e.g. an aggregate when the first weight-4 loader is a propagate) are dropped with a logged warning.

A derived, single-row, aggregate or scanning composite returns the first non-null result of its parts in the given order (later parts are not called); when all return null it returns the plain undefined value (never null).

An item composite reports `isItemTypeSupported(t)` true iff at least one part supports `t`; `loadValue(itemId, ctx)` asks, in order, only the parts supporting the item's type and returns the first non-null result, or the plain undefined value; `preload(ids, ctx)` calls every part's `preload` with just the ids whose type that part supports (possibly an empty list).

Single-row, aggregate, propagate and scanning composites call `preload` on every part with the same arguments and report `isWholeForestDependent()` true iff any part does. A propagate composite's `loadChildren` returns the first non-null function from its parts in order (null if all return null), and `isLoadingSuperRoot()` is true iff any part's is.

`CompositeAttributeLoader.getCompositeCachingStrategy(spec, loaders)` (and a composite's `getCachingStrategy()`) ignores null strategies and returns `MUST_NOT` if any loader has it, else `SHOULD_NOT` if any has it, else `SHOULD` if any has it, else `MAY` (also for an empty collection). Having both `MUST_NOT` and `SHOULD` only logs a warning.

`getCompositeDependencies(loaders)` and `getCompositeContextDependencies(loaders)` return unmodifiable unions of the loaders' non-null attribute dependency sets / context dependency sets (empty, never null, when none declare any); a composite's `getAttributeDependencies()` and `getContextDependencies()` return these.
`getCompositeGlobalTrail(loaders)` returns the union (`TrailItemSet.union`) of the loaders' non-null global trails, or null when none has one; a composite's `getGlobalTrail()` returns it.

`CompositeAttributeLoader.getLoaderClasses(loader)` returns an empty list for null, a one-element list of the loader's class for a non-composite loader, and for a composite the classes of the underlying original loaders (looking through nested composites and adapters), without duplicates, in encounter order.

A `DelegatingAttributeLoader` (any concrete delegating subclass) returns the wrapped loader's `getAttributeSpec()`, `getAttributeDependencies()`, `getContextDependencies()`, `getCachingStrategy()` and `getGlobalTrail()` results unchanged, calling the wrapped loader each time (so a delegating multi-row loader reports the wrapped loader's strategy, not the `SHOULD` default). `delegate()` returns the wrapped instance.
Constructing any delegating loader with a null loader throws NullPointerException; `toString()` is this object's class name (`getClass().getName()`), `:`, and the wrapped loader's `toString()`.
A `DelegatingRowAttributeLoader` forwards `preload(rowIds, forest, ctx)` with the same arguments to the wrapped loader and returns the wrapped loader's `isWholeForestDependent()`.

`DelegatingAggregateAttributeLoader.loadValue(children, ctx)` returns the wrapped aggregate loader's result for the same arguments (including null); preload, whole-forest flag and all properties are forwarded too.
`DelegatingDerivedAttributeLoader.loadValue(ctx)` returns the wrapped derived loader's result for the same context (including null), and its properties are the wrapped loader's.
`DelegatingItemAttributeLoader` forwards `isItemTypeSupported`, `loadValue(itemId, ctx)` (result unchanged) and `preload(ids, ctx)` to the wrapped item loader with the same arguments.
`DelegatingPropagateAttributeLoader.loadChildren(parentValue, parent)` returns the wrapped loader's function (same instance, or null) and `isLoadingSuperRoot()` returns the wrapped loader's answer.
`DelegatingScanningAttributeLoader.loadValue(preceding, ctx)` returns the wrapped scanning loader's result for the same arguments (including null).

`ReducingAggregateLoader` selects its reduction strategy from the spec's `type` parameter at construction (absent means `subtree`); an unknown value such as `sum` throws IllegalArgumentException `unknown strategy type 'sum'`; a null spec throws IllegalArgumentException.

`ReducingAggregateLoader.loadValue(childValues, ctx)` drops the values of children whose row item is a generator or effector (`CoreIdentities.isAutomation(row.getItemId())` over `ctx.getChildren()`, matched by position) before anything else, so their values (even errors) do not take part. The children list and the values list must have the same size.

If any remaining child value is an error, `ReducingAggregateLoader.loadValue` returns the first such value (same instance) without asking for the row's self value; otherwise it returns the strategy's result for the self value (obtained lazily from `getSelfValue`), the remaining child values and this loader as reducer.

`SingleDependencyReducingAggregateLoader` uses `ctx.getDependencyAttributeValue(dependency)` as the row's self value and declares exactly `{dependency}` as attribute dependencies (an immutable singleton).

`ReductionStrategy.getStrategyType(spec)` returns `toString()` of the spec's `type` parameter or `subtree` when absent; `forStrategyType` accepts exactly `children`, `leaves`, `strict`, `subtree` (case-sensitive) and returns the same singleton instance on every call; any other name throws IllegalArgumentException `unknown strategy type '<name>'`, null throws NullPointerException. `forAttributeSpec(spec)` is `forStrategyType(getStrategyType(spec))`.

The `subtree` strategy returns `reducer.merge(self, childValues)` (own value plus children's values, which are themselves subtree totals) wrapped as a value (undefined for null). With `LongSumLoader`: self 5, children 3 and undefined give 8; self undefined and no children give undefined. If the self value is an error, that error value is returned.

The `children` strategy reduces the self values that the children carry as loader data (missing data counts as undefined) and attaches the row's own self value (as an `AttributeValue`, even an error) as loader data of the result: a row's value is the reduction of its direct children's own values, e.g. with `LongSumLoader` children whose own values are 2 and 3 give 5; a leaf gives `reduce` of an empty list (undefined for sums). An error among the carried child self values makes the result that error (still carrying the row's self value). A ClassCastException thrown by the reducer gives an error value.

The `leaves` strategy gives a row with no children `reducer.convert(self)` (by default its own value; an error self value is returned as the error) and a row with children `reducer.reduce` of the children's values, ignoring its own value: with `LongSumLoader` the result is the sum of the own values of the leaves of the subtree.

The `strict` strategy gives a leaf an undefined value carrying, as loader data, its converted self value; a row with children gets the reduction of the values its children carry as loader data (their subtree totals including themselves), and itself carries `merge(self, that result)` as loader data. With `LongSumLoader` a row's value is the sum over its descendants excluding the row itself (leaves undefined). An error carried by a child, or a reducer ClassCastException, gives an error value; an error self value is carried as data and surfaces as the parent's error.

`ValueReducer` is a functional interface (only `reduce(list)` is abstract). Defaults: `convert(self)` returns `self.get()`; `merge(self, reduced)` returns `reduce` of a two-element list `[self.get(), reduced.get()]` (elements may be null); `merge(self, list)` returns `merge(self, () -> reduce(list))`, i.e. reduce of `[self value, reduce(list)]`. Example with a summing reducer: `merge(() -> 1, Arrays.asList(2, 3))` is 6.
